summary:
US final-demand producer prices were unchanged in July, while the unadjusted index rose 4.7 per cent over 12 months. 
Final-demand goods fell 0.7 per cent, led by energy, with thermoplastic resins and materials also lower. 
For textile and apparel supply chains, softer freight and resin signals contrasted with higher services and construction prices.

title: UK's production output flat in Q2; manufacturing rises
summary:
UK production output remained flat quarter on quarter in Q2 2026, after growing 0.2 per cent in Q1, according to ONS. 
Manufacturing rose 1 per cent, while electricity and gas declined 2.3 per cent. 
Monthly production fell 0.2 per cent in June, driven by a 0.5 per cent manufacturing decline, partly offset by a 5.1 per cent rise in mining and quarrying.

title: Textiles, chemicals can fuel India’s aim to be manufacturing hub: Govt
summary:
India’s textile industry can strengthen its global competitiveness by improving raw material availability, scaling up manufacturing through infrastructure support and expanding market access through deeper trade integration, a NITI Aayog report said.

title: Euro area industrial output flat in June as EU production rises 0.2%
summary:

Capital and intermediate goods fell in both regions; Denmark and Croatia led gains; Luxembourg saw the sharpest fall.

title: China's central bank conducts $147.9 bn reverse repo operation
summary:
China’s central bank conducted a 1 trillion yuan (~$147.9 billion) six-month outright reverse repo operation on Friday to maintain ample banking-system liquidity. 
The 185-day operation, maturing on February 15, 2027, will fully roll over an equal amount of repos due in August. 
The PBOC introduced the monthly operations in October 2024 to strengthen its monetary policy toolkit.

title: India's WPI inflation eases to 9.78% in July 2026
summary:

title: Indonesia now faces 10% US reciprocal tariff: Trade Minister Santoso
summary:
US reciprocal tariff on Indonesia is 10 per cent now, the latter’s Trade Minister Budi Santoso said. 
The tariff followed a US Section 301 probe into the use of forced labour. 
After the apex US court annulled the 18-per cent reciprocal tariff initially imposed on Indonesia, a 10-per cent rate was applied to all countries for 150 days, which ended on July 24. 
Indonesia will continue to seek a lower rate.
